node.title: DLI orthogonal Bernoulli-correlation no-go
node.statement: For every r>=1 there are two null events A_r and B_r on 4r independent uniform bits, each defined by r balanced {+1,-1} linear forms, whose row spaces are orthogonal, but P(A_r intersect B_r)/(P(A_r)P(B_r))=(16/9)^r. For power-of-two r, invertible Sylvester-Hadamard mixing presents the same events with every coefficient row dense, flat, and balanced. Thus coordinate independence, coefficient balance/flatness, and orthogonality alone imply no polynomial-loss product correlation bound. This does not falsify the cyclic, nested, primitive-deleted DLI square-root candidate.
node.attack_surface: Check the one-block counts, complete row-space orthogonality, disjoint-block tensorization, Sylvester-Hadamard equivalence, dense row support, integer square-root comparison, and the explicit exclusion of cyclic and primitive DLI structure from the kill scope.
node.falsifier: A mismatch in the exact 6,6,4 one-block counts, a nonzero cross Gram entry, or failure of the r=3 ratio to exceed sqrt(24).
node.notes: This is a proof-architecture fence. A surviving DLI correlation proof must use cyclic phase progression, the nested frequency allocation, antipodal first-owner deletion, or another target-specific input.
